original_interpretation: In June 2021 WSTS forecast the 2021 world semiconductor market at US$527.2 billion (+19.7%); the actual outcome was US$555.9 billion (+26.2%).
evidence_found: WSTS Spring 2021 release (SRC-0230), dated "San Jose, California, on June 08, 2021", p. 2 table: "Total World - $M 440,389 527,223 573,440 6.8 19.7 8.8"; p. 1: "rise ... to outstanding 19.7 percent in the year 2021, which corresponds to a market size of US$ 527 billion." Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223): year block 2021, row "Worldwide", Total Year = 555892514 (thousand US$); 2020 = 440389358; growth 26.2%.
notes: Forecast and outcome both confirmed; the claim clearly labels which is forecast. claim_type estimate acceptable for a mixed forecast/outcome statement.

original_interpretation: WSTS's Spring 2021 and Spring 2022 forecasts were produced without the usual members' forecast meeting because of COVID-19, using an online forecast tool instead.
evidence_found: Spring 2021 release (SRC-0230) p. 1: "Due to the COVID-19 situation, WSTS was unable to have a forecast meeting. This forecast was developed using the online forecast tool by WSTS member companies." Spring 2022 release (SRC-0231) p. 1 opens with the identical two sentences.

original_interpretation: In June 2022 WSTS forecast the 2022 world semiconductor market at US$646.5 billion (+16.3%); the actual outcome was US$574.1 billion (+3.3%).
evidence_found: Spring 2022 release (SRC-0231), dated "June 07, 2022", p. 2 table: "Total World - $M 555,893 646,456 679,650 26.2 16.3 5.1"; p. 1: "a forecast of $646 billion, up 16.3 percent". Outcome: Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223) 2022 Worldwide Total Year = 574084194 thousand US$ (+3.3% vs 555892514); SIA (SRC-0108): "global semiconductor industry sales totaled $574.1 billion in 2022 ... an increase of 3.3%".

original_interpretation: In June 2025 WSTS forecast the 2025 world semiconductor market at US$700.9 billion (+11.2%); the actual outcome was US$795.6 billion (+26.2%).
evidence_found: Spring 2025 release (SRC-0003), dated "June 3, 2025", p. 1: "the global semiconductor market is projected to expand by 11.2% in 2025, reaching a total value of $700.9 billion."; p. 2 table "Total World - $M 630,549 700,874 760,700 19.7 11.2 8.5". Outcome: Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223) 2025 Worldwide Total Year = 795640305 thousand US$; Spring 2026 table (SRC-0001) "Total World - $M 795,640 ... 26.2".

original_interpretation: WSTS's spring forecasts for the current year have missed the outcome by more than 10% in turning points: 2022 was over-forecast by about 13% (US$646.5bn vs US$574.1bn) and 2025 under-forecast by about 12% (US$700.9bn vs US$795.6bn), while 2021 was under-forecast by about 5%.
correction: Say 'in 2022 (a turning point) and 2025 (an acceleration) the spring forecast missed by more than 10%', rather than attributing both to turning points.
notes: Arithmetic correct. Caveats: only three spring vintages (2021, 2022, 2025) were compared, so the generalisation rests on a small sample; and 2025 was an acceleration (+19.7% in 2024 to +26.2% in 2025), not a turning point, so the 'turning points' framing fits 2022 but not 2025.

original_interpretation: SIA's first annual release put 2018 global semiconductor sales at US$468.8 billion (+13.7%), the same as the later WSTS Blue Book figure to one decimal.
evidence_found: SIA, "Monday, February 4, 2019" (SRC-0232): "Global semiconductor industry posted sales of $468.8 billion in 2018, the industry's highest-ever annual total and an increase of 13.7 percent". Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223) 2018 Worldwide Total Year = 468778285 thousand US$ (= 468.8bn to one decimal).
notes: 'First annual release' is the researcher's description of the February SIA release; not contradicted.

original_interpretation: Revisions between SIA's first annual WSTS figure and the later WSTS Blue Book value are small: none for 2018 and 2021, and about +0.5% for 2024 (US$627.6bn to US$630.5bn) and 2025 (US$791.7bn to US$795.6bn).
evidence_found: SIA first releases: 2018 "$468.8 billion" (SRC-0232); 2021 "$555.9 billion" (SRC-0233); 2024 "global semiconductor sales hit $627.6 billion in 2024" (SRC-0054); 2025 "global semiconductor sales hit $791.7 billion in 2025" (SRC-0007). Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223) Total Year: 2018 468778285; 2021 555892514; 2024 630548606; 2025 795640305 (thousand US$). Revisions: 0.0%, 0.0%, +0.47%, +0.50%.
notes: Arithmetic confirmed. Only four years sampled. The Gartner contrast in notes (CLM-0054 to CLM-0053) was not re-checked here.

original_interpretation: SIA's first annual release put 2021 global semiconductor sales at US$555.9 billion, up 26.2% from US$440.4 billion in 2020.
evidence_found: SIA, "Monday, February 14, 2022" (SRC-0233): "Global semiconductor industry sales totaled $555.9 billion in 2021, the highest-ever annual total and an increase of 26.2% compared to the 2020 total of $440.4 billion."

original_interpretation: SIA reported semiconductor sales into China of US$192.5 billion in 2021, up 27.1%, making China the largest single-country market by WSTS region of sale.
evidence_found: SIA 14 Feb 2022 (SRC-0233): "China remained the largest individual market for semiconductors, with sales there totaling $192.5 billion in 2021, an increase of 27.1%."
notes: The 'largest' wording is directly supported by SIA ('largest individual market'). Note China is not one of the four WSTS regions (Americas, Europe, Japan, Asia Pacific); the China figure is an SIA sub-breakdown within Asia Pacific, so 'by WSTS region of sale' should be read as 'on WSTS ship-to data'.

original_interpretation: China accounted for about 56% of WSTS Asia Pacific billings and about 35% of the world market in 2021 (US$192.5bn of US$343.0bn and US$555.9bn).
evidence_found: 192.5 (SIA, SRC-0233) / 342,967 (Asia Pacific 2021, WSTS Spring 2022 table SRC-0231; Blue Book 342967241 thousand US$, SRC-0223) = 56.1%; 192.5 / 555.893 = 34.6%.
notes: Arithmetic confirmed; the vintage mismatch noted by the researcher is immaterial (SIA first-release total 555.9 equals Blue Book 555.893).

original_interpretation: SIA reported 2018 memory sales of US$158.0 billion, up 27.4%, and said sales of all non-memory products combined grew by nearly 8%.
evidence_found: SIA 4 Feb 2019 (SRC-0232): "Memory was the largest semiconductor category by sales with $158.0 billion in 2018, and the fastest growing, with sales increasing 27.4 percent." ... "Even without sales of memory products, sales of all other products combined increased by nearly 8 percent in 2018."

original_interpretation: Memory accounted for roughly 60% of the 2017-2018 increase in the world semiconductor market: memory rose about US$34bn (to US$158.0bn) while the total rose about US$56.6bn.
evidence_found: Recomputed: 158.0/1.274 = 124.0 (SRC-0232); memory change 34.0bn. Blue Book (SRC-0223) Worldwide 2017 = 412220944, 2018 = 468778285 thousand US$; change 56.56bn. 34.0/56.56 = 60.1%. Cross-check: non-memory 2018 = 468.8-158.0 = 310.8 vs 2017 = 412.2-124.0 = 288.2, +7.8%, matching SIA's "nearly 8 percent".
notes: 2017 memory value is implied from the growth rate, as disclosed; the independent cross-check on non-memory growth supports it.

original_interpretation: Memory accounted for about 31% of the 2020-2021 increase in the world semiconductor market (memory +US$36.4bn of a US$115.5bn total increase), so the 2021 boom was broad-based rather than memory-led.
evidence_found: Spring 2021 table (SRC-0230): "Memory 117,482" (2020); Spring 2022 table (SRC-0231): "Memory 153,838" (2021); totals 440,389 and 555,893. Memory +36.36bn of +115.50bn = 31.5%.
notes: Arithmetic confirmed. 'Broad-based rather than memory-led' is a fair reading: Spring 2022 table shows 2021 growth of Analog 33.1%, Logic 30.8%, Memory 30.9%, Discrete 27.4%.

original_interpretation: In 2022 memory sales fell by about US$24bn (from US$153.8bn to about US$130bn) while the world market still grew about US$18bn, so non-memory products grew by roughly US$42bn.
evidence_found: SIA (SRC-0108): "memory ($130 billion) were the largest semiconductor categories by sales" (2022); "global semiconductor industry sales totaled $574.1 billion in 2022 ... an increase of 3.3%". Spring 2022 table (SRC-0231) Memory 2021 = 153,838; Blue Book 2021/2022 totals 555,893 / 574,084. Memory -23.8bn, total +18.2bn, non-memory +42.0bn.
notes: Arithmetic confirmed; memory 2022 figure is rounded ('$130 billion') so non-memory growth is approximate, as the claim says.

original_interpretation: Memory accounted for about 71% of the 2023-2024 increase in the world semiconductor market (memory +US$73.2bn of a US$103.7bn total increase).
evidence_found: Spring 2025 table (SRC-0003): "Memory 165,516 ... 79.3" (2024 value and 2024 growth); implied 2023 memory = 165,516/1.793 = 92.3bn, matching CLM-0290. Blue Book (SRC-0223) Worldwide 2023 = 526885425, 2024 = 630548606 thousand US$. Memory +73.2bn of +103.7bn = 70.6%.
notes: 2023 memory confirmed independently via WSTS's own 79.3% growth rate rather than only the SIA release.

original_interpretation: Memory accounted for about 39% of the 2024-2025 increase in the world semiconductor market (memory +US$64.5bn of a US$165.1bn increase); logic contributed most of the rest.
evidence_found: Spring 2025 table (SRC-0003): Memory 2024 165,516; Logic 2024 215,768. Spring 2026 table (SRC-0001): "Logic 299,547 ... 38.8", "Memory 230,042 ... 39.0", "Total World - $M 795,640 ... 26.2". Memory +64.5bn, Logic +83.8bn, total +165.1bn; memory share 39.1%, logic 50.7% of the increase (83% of the non-memory remainder).

original_interpretation: In WSTS's Spring 2026 forecast, memory accounts for about 80% of the forecast 2025-2026 increase (memory +US$574bn of a roughly US$714bn increase).
notes: Using the table total (1,511,248) the increase is US$715.6bn rather than the claim's 'roughly US$714bn' (which used the rounded 1.51tn); share is still about 80%. Forecast, as the claim states.

original_interpretation: Year-to-year swings in the headline chip market are dominated by memory prices in memory up-cycles (2018, 2024, 2026) and down-cycles (2019, 2023), so a market-size change says little about unit demand or non-memory businesses unless memory is separated out.
evidence_found: Memory share of the change in the WSTS total: 2018 ~60% (SRC-0232, SRC-0223); 2019: SIA (SRC-0378) "Sales of memory products were down significantly in 2019 by dollar value, decreasing 32.6 percent compared to 2018" and total "$412.1 billion in 2019, a decrease of 12.1 percent" -> memory about -51.5bn of a -56.5bn fall (~91%); 2023: memory 130 -> 92.3 (-37.7bn) of total 574.1 -> 526.9 (-47.2bn) (~80%); 2024 ~71% (SRC-0003); 2026 forecast ~80% (SRC-0001).
correction: Replace 'memory prices' with 'memory revenue' unless a price/volume decomposition is cited; flag 2026 as forecast.
notes: Memory dominates the dollar change in each named year, so the core reading is supported. Caveats: (1) 2026 is a forecast, not an outcome; (2) the sources give memory revenue, not a price/volume split, so attributing the swings specifically to memory prices is not evidenced here (SIA/WSTS releases do not decompose price vs units); (3) in non-memory-cycle years (2021, 2025) memory was only 31-39% of the change.

original_interpretation: Asia Pacific's share of WSTS world billings rose from 7.8% in 1986 to 25.1% in 2000, 53.6% in 2010 and a peak of 62.5% in 2019, then fell to 55.3% in 2025.
evidence_found: "All numbers are in 1000 US$." (sheet 'Monthly Data', row 3); column N "Total Year" (row 4). Asia Pacific / Worldwide Total Year: 1986 2052314/26355359 = 7.8%; 2000 = 25.1%; 2010 = 53.6%; 2019 257878591/412306976 = 62.5% (highest share of any year 1986-2025); 2025 439746582/795640305 = 55.3%.
notes: All five shares and the 2019 peak recomputed from the July 2026 XLSX.

original_interpretation: Japan was the largest WSTS region every year from 1986 to 1992 (39.7% of world billings in 1986), was overtaken by the Americas in 1993, and fell to 5.6% of world billings in 2025.
evidence_found: "All numbers are in 1000 US$." (sheet 'Monthly Data', row 3); column N "Total Year" (row 4). Japan exceeds every other region each year 1986-1992 (e.g. 1992 Japan 19396118 vs Americas 18410756); 1993 Japan 23798388 < Americas 24744008; 1986 Japan 10450725/26355359 = 39.7%; 2025 Japan 44723219/795640305 = 5.6%.

original_interpretation: The Americas' share of WSTS world billings rose from 19.1% in 2019 to 32.2% in 2025, the sharpest regional shift in the series, coinciding with AI data-centre build-out.
evidence_found: "All numbers are in 1000 US$." (sheet 'Monthly Data', row 3); column N "Total Year" (row 4). Americas share: 2019 78619471/412306976 = 19.1%; 2025 256476450/795640305 = 32.2% (+13.1pp). Comparable six-year shifts in the same series: Asia Pacific 2000-2006 +21.9pp (25.1% to 47.0%), 1999-2005 +20.6pp; Japan 1991-1997 -15.0pp.
correction: Americas' share rose from 19.1% (2019) to 32.2% (2025), the largest rise for the Americas in the series, but smaller than Asia Pacific's +21.9pp gain in 2000-2006.
notes: The two share values are correct and 2019-2025 is the largest six-year rise in the Americas' share in the series. But it is not 'the sharpest regional shift in the series': Asia Pacific's share rose 21.9pp in 2000-2006 and Japan's fell 15.0pp in 1991-1997. The AI data-centre link is interpretation (the researcher's note says so).

original_interpretation: Because WSTS assigns sales to the customer's ship-to location, the rise of Asia Pacific mainly tracks the migration of electronics assembly (contract manufacturers and ODMs) to Asia, not where chips are designed, made or finally consumed.
evidence_found: SIA market-data page (new source @sia_md): shipments are "broken down by semiconductor product type, end-use, and region of shipment to end-customer, distributor, or consignee when possible". Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223) shows Asia Pacific share rising from 7.8% (1986) to 62.5% (2019).
notes: The ship-to basis of WSTS regions is supported, so regional data do not show where chips are designed or finally consumed. The causal claim that the rise 'mainly tracks' migration of electronics assembly to Asia is plausible but no source checked here quantifies it; it remains interpretation.

original_interpretation: In the WSTS series 1986-2025 the largest annual decline was -32.0% in 2001 (US$204.4bn to US$139.0bn) and the largest annual increase was +41.7% in 1995; the market fell in 1996, 1998, 2001, 2008, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2019 and 2023.
WSTS billings for January-July 2026 totalled US$861.1 billion, already above the full-year 2025 total of US$795.6 billion.
evidence_found: Blue Book XLSX (SRC-0223, file WSTS-Historical-Billings-Report-Jul_2026.xlsx, sheet 'Monthly Data', units "All numbers are in 1000 US$."), year block 2026, row "Worldwide": Jan 82925862, Feb 103671953, Mar 118321116, Apr 115800518, May 140466438, Jun 157462968, Jul 142480424; "Total Year" 861129279; Aug-Dec blank. 2025 Total Year 795640305.
notes: Jan-Jul monthly values sum exactly to the Total Year cell. Monthly data are subject to revision.

original_interpretation: January-July 2026 WSTS billings were about 110% higher than in January-July 2025 (US$861.1bn vs US$409.1bn).
Gartner's preliminary estimate (January 2023) put 2022 worldwide semiconductor revenue at US$601.7 billion, up 1.1% from US$595 billion in 2021.
evidence_found: Electronics Online, "Thursday, 19 January, 2023" (SRC-0240): "worldwide semiconductor revenue increased 1.1% in 2022 to total $601.7 billion, up from $595 billion in 2021", attributed to preliminary results by Gartner.
notes: Secondary (trade press) report of a Gartner preliminary release; industry_press classification and estimate claim_type are honest. Superseded by Gartner's April 2023 revision (CLM-0701), which the claim set already records.

original_interpretation: Gartner's revised figure (April 2023) put 2022 worldwide semiconductor revenue at US$599.6 billion, growth of 0.2%.
evidence_found: Gartner, "April 26, 2023" (SRC-0234): "In 2022, the market totaled $599.6 billion, which was marginal growth of 0.2% from 2021."; "Table 1. Semiconductor Revenue Forecast, Worldwide, 2022-2024 (Billions of U.S. Dollars)" 2022 Revenue 599.6, Growth 0.2; "Source: Gartner (April 2023)".
notes: URL is Gartner's gcom.pdo.aws mirror of its newsroom; content is Gartner's own release.

original_interpretation: Gartner's April 2026 forecast release put 2025 worldwide semiconductor revenue at US$805.3 billion (memory US$216.3bn, non-memory US$589.0bn), up from its preliminary US$793 billion.
evidence_found: Gartner, "STAMFORD, Conn., April 8, 2026" (SRC-0236), Table 1: Memory 216.3, Nonmemory 589.0, Total Market 805.3 (2025 column); "Source: Gartner (April 2026)". The page does not mention US$793bn. Gartner, January 12, 2026 (SRC-0235): "Worldwide semiconductor revenue totaled $793 billion in 2025, an increase of 21% year-over-year (YoY), according to preliminary results by Gartner, Inc."
correction: Cite SRC-0235 for the preliminary US$793bn figure; SRC-0236 supports only the 805.3 / 216.3 / 589.0 split.
notes: All numbers are correct, but the 'preliminary US$793 billion' comparison is not in the cited source (SRC-0236); it comes from Gartner's January 2026 release (SRC-0235), which should be added to source_ids.

original_interpretation: In April 2026 Gartner forecast 2026 worldwide semiconductor revenue at US$1,320.2 billion (+64%), with memory at US$633.3 billion, and 2027 at US$1,554.5 billion.
evidence_found: Gartner 8 Apr 2026 (SRC-0236): "Global semiconductor revenue is projected to exceed $1.3 trillion in 2026"; "Gartner forecasts semiconductor revenue will grow 64% in 2026"; Table 1: Memory 633.3 (2026), 748.1 (2027); Nonmemory 686.9, 806.4; Total Market 1,320.2 (2026), 1,554.5 (2027); "Source: Gartner (April 2026)".
notes: 1,320.2/805.3 = +63.9%. Forecast, correctly typed as estimate. Note Gartner (US$1.32tn) and WSTS Spring 2026 (US$1.51tn, SRC-0001) 2026 forecasts differ by ~US$190bn; different populations and vintages.
